events.line: A coach party from Barnsley descends, all hungry, all wanting to know if the peas are mushy. They are. Double takings.
A storm takes the power out for the day. You sell nothing and eat the leftovers by torchlight.
The gulls get at the queue. Customers leave quicker than the chips do.
A man with a notebook orders cod and chips and says 'hm' four times. Word gets around: a good day.
A summer bank holiday. The queue goes round the corner and stops to ask what the queue is for.
A rival chippy opens at the end of the road with a banner and a free scraps offer. Trade is down until the novelty wears off.

upgrades.name: A second fryer
upgrades.text: Twice the chips an hour, and twice the oil to heat.

upgrades.name: A ten-year lease on the quay
upgrades.text: Nobody puts the rent up on the trade you built. The council likes you less for it.

upgrades.name: A late-night licence
upgrades.text: Open until the pubs turn out. The pubs turn out loud.

asks.title: The Goth Weekend
asks.text: It is the Whitby Goth Weekend, and the pavement outside {deed} is full of people in black who are, you find, extremely polite and very hungry.

options.label: Stay open until midnight
options.say: Midnight comes and goes in a queue of velvet and eyeliner. They tip in coins and compliments.

risk.say: Rain at ten, and the queue goes with it. You fry for the seagulls.

options.label: Open the usual hours and put a menu board out
options.say: A good steady weekend, and not one complaint about the peas.

options.label: Put the sign on 'closed' and go to the pictures
options.say: You miss the best weekend of the year. Somebody else's chips sell very well.
